sentences.text: ORAL ORDER
The petitioner has filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking just and proper compensation for injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
When the matter was set for arguments, the petitioner/claimant filed an application to recall and reopen the case in order to examine an eyewitness to the accident.
The Trial Court rejected the application, stating that it was filed merely to delay the proceedings.

2. Learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company submitted that, since the petitioner filed the NC: 2024:KHC:45260 application at the argument stage, the Tribunal was justified in rejecting the application.

Smt. Kamalasanthosh vs Rudresh C on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109221487/
2 3.
The petitioner, in order to establish that he sustained injuries in the road traffic accident, seeks to examine an alleged eyewitness to the accident.
If the petitioner is not allowed to examine the alleged eyewitness, he may be deprived of just and proper compensation.
Conversely, no prejudice will be caused to the respondent- Insurance Company if the petitioner is permitted to reopen the case and examine the alleged eyewitness.
Accordingly, I issue the following:
ORDER i. The writ petition is allowed.

ii. The impugned order dated 28.07.2023 passed by the VII Additional District Judge and Member, MACT, Tumakuru, in MVC No. 1202/2019 on the application filed under Section 151 of CPC, is hereby quashed, and consequently, the application is allowed.

sentences.text: iii. The Tribunal is directed to permit the petitioner to examine any eyewitness to the accident.
